## Locate tensor rows, faces and ghost slabs (`NMASS` / `PartOptions`) {#sec-ch01-layout}

### Summary

Every field of a block is one tensor with the same shape. There is a variable axis, then the three space axes in the
order $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$, so that $x_1$ is the fastest-varying one. The tensor layout is the index order
(variable, $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$), with the ghost cells included in each space extent. A direction with more than one cell carries ghost
cells on both sides; a one-cell direction has none. This section says which row is which variable, where the interior
starts and ends, how a face pair is stored, and how a slab of a block is addressed.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: rows, axes, interior ends, face pairs and the slab selector `part`.

**Data.** The hydro tensors (variable, $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$); `il`, `iu` are the first and last interior index.

**Placement.** Everywhere a kernel indexes a block tensor.

**Activation.** `NMASS` must be 0 (default); `PartOptions` selects exterior slabs by default.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; no convergence order.

**Evidence.** `test_scalar.<b>` (shape, exact), `test_mesh_exchange_python` (ghost slab, exact); see Tests.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The row indices are the enumeration of {{< code src/snap.h >}}: density `IDN` = 0, the three velocity or momentum rows
`IVX`, `IVY`, `IVZ` = 1, 2, 3. The pressure or energy row is `IPR` = 4 and the first species row `ICY` = 5. The face
pair slots are `ILT` = 0 and `IRT` = 1. The primitive and conserved rows share the same indices with different
meanings. The static assertion of the same file refuses the legacy `NMASS > 0` layout. The cell counts are `nc1`,
`nc2`, `nc3` of `CoordinateOptionsImpl` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl >}}): the interior
count plus twice `nghost` when the direction is resolved, 1 otherwise. The interior ends are `il` and `iu` of
`CoordinateImpl` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl >}}), `nghost` and `nghost + nx1 - 1`, or 0 on a
one-cell axis. At a face the left and right reconstructed states share the face index. `_apply_inplace`
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp _apply_inplace >}}) writes the two output slices offset by one cell and copies the
end values into the ghosts. `PartOptions` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.hpp PartOptions >}}) selects `exterior`
(default true), per-direction extensions, a `depth`[^rg-1a50597f1fee] and the number of dimensions. `MeshBlockImpl::part`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::part >}}) takes an offset triple in $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$ order and
returns the interior or the boundary slab on that side. Layout has no convergence order.

@fig-ch01-layout-flow shows the storage stencil.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-layout-flow
#| fig-cap: "A lower-wall storage stencil. Blue circles are cell averages, orange triangles are face states, the hatched cell is a ghost and the thick black line is the physical wall. The shared face index holds both reconstructed states."
#| fig-alt: "Cells i-1, i and i+1, with i-1 a ghost and the wall at face i-1/2."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_layout_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the layout is fixed this way.** Three facts of the code.

1. $x_1$ is the last axis, so a column is contiguous in memory; the shape check of `initialize_local` requires
   (variables, $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$) ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}).
2. A one-cell axis carries no ghosts, so a two-dimensional run stores no empty slabs
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl >}}).
3. The two reconstructed states of a face share one face index, so the face pair can be passed to a Riemann solver as
   one tensor. `_apply_inplace` writes them offset by one cell
   ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp _apply_inplace >}}).

: Implementation anchors for the storage layout. {#tbl-ch01-layout-code}

1. Rows and the index assertion: `ICY` in {{< code src/snap.h >}}.
2. Counts and ends: `nc1` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl >}}), `il`
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl >}}).
3. Slabs and face pairs: `part` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::part >}}), `_apply_inplace`
   ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp _apply_inplace >}}).

**How to use it.** Index a block tensor by row and by slab, never by hand-computed offsets:

```cpp
auto interior = pmb->part({0, 0, 0}, PartOptions().exterior(false));   // the owned cells
auto lower_x1 = pmb->part({0, 0, -1}, PartOptions().exterior(true));   // the x1 ghost slab below
auto rho_d = hydro_u[IDN];                                              // one row
```

`part` takes the offset triple in $x_3$, $x_2$, $x_1$ order ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::part >}}).
Refused: a build with `NMASS > 0`, by the static assertion of {{< code src/snap.h >}}. The row enumeration is:

```cpp
enum {
  // hydro variables
  IDN = 0,  //!< Density index
  IVX = 1,  //!< X-velocity index
  IVY = 2,  //!< Y-velocity index
  IVZ = 3,  //!< Z-velocity index
  IPR = 4,  //!< Pressure index
  ICY = 5,  //!< Composition/species index (first mass fraction)

  // reconstruction variables
  ILT = 0,  //!< Left interface
  IRT = 1,  //!< Right interface
};
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_scalar.<b>` | the scalar tensors have the block's shape, device and dtype | exact | the API contract |
| `test_mesh_exchange_python` | the selected ghost slab of each block holds its neighbour's rank | exact equality | an integer rank field is copied |

: Source assertions for the storage layout. {#tbl-ch01-layout-tests}

The assertions are {{< code tests/test_scalar.cpp DeviceTest.initialize_and_transport_scalar >}} and the
top-level `assert` of {{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}.

Both tests run on CPU (`test_scalar.<b>` also on CUDA through the shared device list). Neither has been run
for this report at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**. No report check exists for this section.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`NMASS > 0` is refused by the species-layout static assertion. A one-cell axis cannot supply a multi-cell
stencil. The tests exercise selected shapes and slabs, not every depth and extension combination.
:::

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-1a50597f1fee]: depth — `PartOptions` field: how many cells deep a selected slab reaches (default 99)
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
